children: Pet Valu is seeing early signs of a rebound in discretionary pet supplies after more than three years of consumer belt-tightening. On an earnings call, CEO Greg Ramier points to the chain's hardlines segment, which includes durable goods such as toys, collars, and crates, as a standout. He calls it "the strongest results we've seen since early 2023." The improvement in 3Q was led by a pickup in toy sales and he says this is expanding into subcategories such as waste management, collars and leashes. CFO Linda Drysdale adds that the trend has helped to narrow the gap "to the consistent growth we are seeing in consumables." (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)
